The two countries are celebrating 55 years of diplomatic relations. Meanwhile, Austrian companies continue expanding their presence in the Chinese market and seeking new opportunities for business development.
items.title: Austrian Companies Strengthen Ties With China Amid Trade Growth

items.summary: Festivals in India, marked by firecrackers, coloured powders, processions and gatherings along riverbanks, bring together large numbers of people but also expand their environmental footprint. Fireworks release particulate matter such as PM2.5 and PM10, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and metallic compounds including barium and aluminium; the concern is especially around fine particles that reach deep into the lungs. Dr Abhishek Agrawal, a medical officer at a government hospital, explains how exposure can cause coughing, throat irritation, breathlessness and worsening respiratory symptoms, with children, the elderly and people with asthma or COPD being most vulnerable. Pollution may persist after celebrations end due to low wind speeds and temperature inversions during the post-monsoon period. Beyond the lungs, pollution is linked to higher blood pressure, irregular heart rhythms and cardiovascular complications, plus headaches, stress and hearing damage from noise.
items.title: India's Festive Pollution Threatens Health and Environment

items.summary: Expelled JD(U) leader Anant Singh said invitations for his daughter's grand wedding are being sent across India and Pakistan, saying political differences have no place at family celebrations. He would invite leaders beyond party lines, including Nitish Kumar and Lalu Prasad Yadav. The event comes as Singh faces a turbulent period after expulsion from the JD(U) with his wife Neelam Devi over alleged anti-party activities in October.
items.title: JD(U)'s Anant Singh Opens Daughter's Wedding Invitations Across Borders

items.summary: At the China Pavilion during the ninth China International Import Expo in Shanghai, visitors could take the controls of a CR450 high-speed train simulator. The console recreated the prototype's controls, sights and sounds so guests experienced the driver's seat without leaving the expo floor. According to China Railway, the CR450 prototype reached kilometers per hour on its test track.
items.title: Visitors Take Controls of CR450 Simulator at CIIE 2026

items.summary: Tong'an Bay, once Xiamen's largest urban bay and a fishing ground, suffered ecological decline from unregulated aquaculture and wastewater discharge. Around 2015, more than 40,000 fishermen transitioned away as operations phased out and tidal flats were dredged. More than 200 million cubic meters of sediment were removed, increasing tidal capacity by over 40 million cubic meters and improving water exchange around 30%. In 2017 Xiamen launched a coastal new town project alongside the Huandong Romantic Line, a 50.6-kilometer ecological corridor now a popular tourism landmark.
items.title: Xiamen Transforms Polluted Tong'an Bay Into Coastal Tourism Destination

items.summary: The article argues that Tesla has not produced a successful new product launch since JB Straubel stepped down as chief technology officer in July 2019. It points to the Cybertruck, which it calls an epic failure: installed tooling for 125k units yearly yet sold only 70k over three years after spending $2bn on research and development while making just $100m gross profit, leaving a net project loss of around $2 billion. The author admits not fact-checking these figures but notes Tesla planned far higher output—up to 500,000 units. After Straubel's departure came the Model Y in March 2019 and later the Cybercab; no other major launch followed. The piece speculates on leadership dynamics without knowing why Straubel left or how much he influenced product development. It adds that whether the Cybercab becomes a success remains to be seen, and it carries uncertainty about Tesla's internal decisions throughout.
items.title: Tesla's Product Launches Since CTO Straubel Departed

items.summary: Public bodies across the UK report being swamped by a flood of AI-generated correspondence, dubbed “AI clog” and described by researchers as “agentic flooding.” Labour MP’s-office caseworker Hollie Wickens says half their emails are now AI. The Information Commissioner’s Office found many authorities received more requests in 2025; complaint length rose from about two pages to roughly ten times longer, with one reaching around 200 pages. Employment tribunal claims opened by single claimants jumped 28% to 14,000 cases between April and June, leaving 70,000 open at the end of that quarter. Transport for London recorded a record 4,769 freedom of information requests in 2025-26, up 5% on its prior peak.
items.title: UK public bodies overwhelmed by AI-generated complaints

items.summary: A few months after a John Galliano retrospective was cancelled amid backlash over the designer's past, the Costume Institute announced its next Met Gala theme as extraORDINARY: fashion and the poetics of the everyday. The gala is scheduled for 3 May 2027, with the dress code traditionally drawn from the exhibition theme. A press release says it will explore how designers rework familiar garments and commonplace materials such as jeans, T-shirts, puffer coats, paper, plastic and metal. Reactions are mixed: Dana Thomas calls it tone deaf and a missed opportunity to honour late figures like Dolly Parton and Bob Mackie, while stylist Marian Kwei describes the theme as clever and an interesting celebration of fashion design. Some commentators note its distance from Galliano's fantastical work. The article notes red-carpet precedents for denim, including Da'vine Joy Randolph in 2024 wearing an all-denim creation by Zac Posen, and Troye Sivan and Bhavitha Mandava at last year's event.
items.title: Met Gala Adopts Everyday-Fashion Theme Amid Mixed Reactions

items.summary: Traders claim they have been priced out of Liverpool's Christmas market after a new operator, Underbelly, took over running it. Anthony Grice said he was quoted £12,000 for a stall at St George's Plateau. Jeweller Alex Healy said her smallest hut would cost between £14,000 and £15,000, which she cannot afford despite the cost-of-living crisis affecting her customers. Council leader Liam Robinson met traders to understand their challenges.
items.title: Christmas market traders say new operator's prices are unaffordable

items.summary: Banana producers in Latin America are calling for better pay to help cope with the impact of the climate crisis, as they face big drops in production resulting from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event. High winds in parts of Colombia and heavy rainfall in Peru and Ecuador are already affecting production, according to the Fairtrade Foundation ethical trade body. During the previous El Niño cycle, productivity across its farmers dropped by 13% in the Dominican Republic, 22% in Ecuador, and 6% in Peru compared with the year before.
items.title: Latin American banana producers demand fairer pay amid climate crisis

items.summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi revisited her early memories of celebrating Diwali in a conversation featured on video, sharing reminiscences about the festival's traditions and festivities. She reminisced that diyas lit nearly every corner of the residence, around the pond, veranda and pathways, while an idol of Lord Ganesh stood at the entrance where the family lit its first diya. Her daughter Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also appeared in the conversation.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi recalls Diwali celebrations with family

items.summary: President Isaac Herzog has tasked Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, with forming a new government after last month's legislative elections produced no clear winner. A statement from the president's office announced the decision following consultations with political figures including Netanyahu. Factions backing Eisenkot totalled 67 Knesset members versus 46 for Netanyahu. Both blocs fell short of a majority in the 120-seat parliament, prompting calls for unity talks.
items.title: Eisenkot Named to Form Israeli Government After No Clear Winner

items.summary: The Jillaroos qualified for a fifth consecutive Rugby League World Cup final, defeating Fiji 34-14. Despite an early scare with an 8-0 first-half lead by Fiji, Australia recovered to advance. The team will face New Zealand next Sunday in the decider at Lang Park.
items.title: Jillaroos Overcome Fiji Scare in World Cup Final Qualification

items.summary: The Gadag District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ordered Kittur Rani Chennamma Urban Credit Souhardha Sahakari Ltd. to repay two customers Rs 17,63,274 of principal stuck in fixed deposits, savings and recurring accounts after their repayment demands failed. The society denied deficiency in service; the commission rejected that objection for lack of evidence and awarded interest plus Rs 20,000 compensation and Rs 5,000 litigation costs. Payment is due within eight weeks.
items.title: Consumer Commission Orders Credit Society to Repay Depositors

items.summary: A masked man in military clothing drove a car into Krakow's Main Market Square and opened fire on Saturday afternoon, killing six people and injuring 16. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it an act of terrorism. The suspect, a 24-year-old Polish citizen with no prior convictions but a firearms licence, was wounded and detained after an exchange of fire. A two-day national mourning began at midnight Sunday.
items.title: Krakow shooting leaves six dead; mourning declared

items.summary: Luca Van Assche lost the Paris Masters semi-final to Ben Shelton, losing 5-7 6-3 6-4. The 22-year-old Frenchman reached his first Paris final since 2008 for a French player and will rise to a career-high ranking of 34th when Monday's rankings are published. He said the run gave him more self-confidence, knowing he can reach a semi-final.
items.title: Van Assche ends Paris Masters run with boosted confidence after semi-final loss

items.summary: A Sunday book pick reviews John Gray’s 2020 book, Feline Philosophy: Cats and the Meaning of Life (Penguin Random House), which argues that cats teach humans about living well. The reviewer summarizes Gray’s six-chapter case that felines live by following their nature while humans suppress theirs, framing cats as morally superior because they lack ideas and remain untroubled by death. Gray is described as a long-time cat devotee who has owned the animals for more than 30 years. The review notes his historical examples of violence against cats and Eastern faiths that revere them, ending with his ten commandments on behalf of the animal.
items.title: Book Review Frames Cats as Moral and Existential Superiors

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath defended his sister after a viral video showed her running a tea shop, saying she was pursuing financial independence and living respectably. He said the 25 crore people of Uttar Pradesh are his family and that everyone should stand on their own two feet rather than beg.
items.title: Yogi Adityanath Defends Sister's Tea Shop Work

items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said it ran a two-month enforcement drive from September 1 to November 5, inspecting 56,431 establishments and issuing 10,047 improvement notices. It seized more than 3,270 metric tonnes of food worth an estimated ₹81.8 crore and suspended over 1,100 licences while cancelling 52 and sealing 314 establishments. The regulator said it would keep working with State Food Safety Authorities to uphold safety standards.
items.title: FSSAI Seizes Food Worth ₹81.8 Crore, Suspends Licences in Enforcement Drive

items.summary: COP31, the 31st Conference of the Parties under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, opens Monday (Nov. 9) and runs through Nov. 20 in Antalya, Türkiye, which will preside over the annual summit. The venue spans about 1.1 million square meters (11.8 million sq ft), organized around dialogue, consensus, and action under the theme COP of the Future – COP of Implementation. Official negotiations occur in the Blue Zone; public engagement happens in the Green Zone. Facilities include halls named after Anatolian landmarks, a Zero Waste Museum, butterfly garden, and 630 low-emission buses for participants, with roughly 27,957 security personnel deployed across five medical stations and seven ambulances to support emergency response.
items.title: Türkiye Opens COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya

items.summary: France have named a reshuffled 42-man squad of seven new players ahead of their Nations Championship match against South Africa, following a 54-17 win over Fiji in Lyon on Saturday. The selection includes Teddy Thomas's return after five years and Gael Fickou, who could reach 100 caps. Flyhalf Romain Ntamack is unavailable due to a left shoulder injury sustained during the test.
items.title: France call up seven players for Springboks clash with Ntamack ruled out

items.summary: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Saturday took a swipe at Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president KT Rama Rao, saying “simply growing a beard does not make you look like Revanth Reddy.” He added that imitation would not earn KTR the trust of voters and compared substanceless posturing to a fox trying to become a tiger. The jibe is part of an ongoing Congress–BRS war of words over governance in Telangana, which has included allegations about irrigation projects and disinformation on Godavari water. There was no immediate comment from Rao or the BRS at filing time.
items.title: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy Jabs KTR Over Imitating His Looks

items.summary: Samco Securities named ten stocks for the upcoming fiscal year, including BSE, Adani Power, MCX, TechM, HFCL and others. It relies on its rule-based approach with disciplined profit-booking and stop-losses, advising investors to follow risk-management levels as targets may change. For Adani Power it cites a record Q2FY27 quarter with 141.5 per cent profit growth, then recommends buying at Rs 186-192 with a target of up to Rs 318.85 over one year.
items.title: Samco Names Adani Power Among Top Samvat 2083 Picks

items.summary: Bangladesh's Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman called ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina a 'convicted criminal,' convicted by the tribunal of crimes against humanity during the July-August 2024 uprising, sentenced to death on one charge and life imprisonment on another. Dhaka has requested India extradite her under their extradition treaty and will follow due legal process without emotion. Hasina fled Bangladesh for India on August 5, 2024, after a mass uprising ended her 15-year rule; an interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus took charge.
items.title: Bangladesh Law Minister Labels Hasina a Convicted Criminal and Demands Her Return

items.summary: The UAE National Guard said Sunday it rescued 22 people after a fire broke out on a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman. The rescued Arab nationals were all reported to be in stable condition, according to Emirati authorities. They received first aid before being handed over to relevant authorities.
items.title: UAE National Guard Rescues 22 After Cargo Ship Fire in Gulf of Oman

items.summary: The Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer admitted on Saturday that multiple Elector Photo Identity Card numbers were inadvertently generated for the same person during a special intensive revision of electoral rolls. The clarification followed a report by The Hindu finding 803 voter IDs linked to just 397 persons in Mahadevapura Assembly constituency, plus duplicate IDs across constituencies from pending deletion applications after migration. Officials said cases have been referred to district election officers for verification and remedial action under the law. More than 99. 3 lakh voters were deleted from Karnataka's final list published on October 27, with voter numbers falling to 4.
items.title: Karnataka Admits Duplicate Voter IDs in Roll Revision

items.summary: The Japan Coast Guard announced that the “Godzilla Megamullion,” a seafloor formation discovered in 2001, has been selected for the International Union of Geological Sciences’ list of 100 Geological Heritage Sites. Measuring about 125 kilometers long and 55 kilometers wide—roughly 10 times larger than typical—the site is believed to be the largest megamullion ever found and was registered internationally in 2021.
items.title: Japan Coast Guard Names Godzilla Megamullion Geological Heritage Site

items.summary: A 55-year-old scooter rider, Santosh Singh Chauhan, was killed Saturday evening near his home in Kalyanpur area of Kanpur when a speeding Mahindra Thar collided with him. The impact reportedly dragged the rider for about 25 to 30 metres before the vehicle broke through a residential boundary wall. Police reached after receiving information and registered a case following a complaint from the family, while examining CCTV footage; the driver's identity remains unestablished.
items.title: Scooter rider killed after speeding Thar collision on Diwali eve in Kanpur

items.summary: A brokerage upgraded shares of Tata Steel, Hindalco and Power Grid to 'Buy' and raised target prices. Nuvama's estimate for Tata Steel was Rs 9,900 crore; the company reported standalone EBITDA of Rs 10,320 crore in Q2 FY27, up 9.6 per cent sequentially. Hindalco India, including Utkal Alumina, posted EBITDA of Rs 8,450 crore against an estimate of Rs 7,080 crore. The article was published on Nov 8, 2026.
items.title: Nuvama Upgrades Tata Steel, Hindalco and Power Grid Shares

items.summary: The South Australian government will introduce legislation banning councils from issuing ticketless parking fines after a camera car passes, requiring inspectors to physically issue tickets. The Local Government Association of SA said it was not consulted and argued the technology improves efficiency. Premier Mr Malinauskas said AI could still be used but any ticket must be issued by an inspector at the time of the offence.
items.title: SA government plans ban on ticketless parking fines

items.summary: Talib Ahmed Bensouda filed candidacy papers for Gambia's December 5 presidential election, where incumbent Adama Barrow seeks a third term. The move follows a government report accusing the former Kanifing mayor of financial improprieties and abuse of office; his UNITE party rejected these as political manoeuvring and blamed the NPP government on national blackouts that have fueled protests.
items.title: Gambian opposition leader files for presidential election amid abuse allegations

items.summary: At 80, British designer Paul Smith spent a Saturday afternoon helping visitors at the Mayfair store of his label. He attended to guests from Norway, Greece, Canada and Mexico without revealing himself as the famous designer. The interview coincides with the publication of his memoir Threads: My Life in Style, which he frames less as nostalgia than as proof that old-fashioned success is still possible through hard work and curiosity. Smith says his partner Pauline raised his standards on quality. He notes that since air conditioning and travel introduced lighter Spanish and Italian fabrics, British style has become more international while keeping a playful accent. His empire now spans 130 stores, including 20 in Japan, employs more than 1,200 people, and posted earnings of more than €235 million ($264 million) in its most profitable year.
items.title: Paul Smith, at 80, still serves shoppers in his London flagship

items.summary: Palmer Luckey, founder of Oculus and Anduril Industries, and Ben Lamm, founder of Colossal Biosciences, have formed a new company called Warhound. According to the Financial Times, reported through EL PAÍS USA Edition, the venture aims to combine genetic-engineering expertise with defense technology to design, breed and train canine units for military, law-enforcement and emergency-response teams, reducing reliance on dogs bred in Europe. The company is reportedly valued at $1.2 billion after raising $200 million in seed funding. Neither founder will run the firm daily; David Spirk has been recruited as chief executive officer.
items.title: Luckey and Lamm Launch Warhound to Build Elite Military Dogs

items.summary: After Republicans lost control of the House and Senate plus governorships and state legislatures, including red states like Texas and Kansas where they had long held power, analysts describe a shattered coalition that powered Donald Trump to three straight nominations. Outgoing Florida Governor Ron DeSantis called it close to an extinction-level event for the party, while Vice-President JD Vance blamed public anger over the war with Iran and predicted infighting. A New York Times analysis of voter data found Latino support for Democratic candidates rose 29 percentage points from 2024-26, and young voters aged 18-29 increased by 33 points. Strategists say it is too early to tell which faction will win out ahead of 2028.
items.title: Republicans Reassess After Trump Coalition Collapse in Midterms

items.summary:
The burned-out ruins of Kehlsteinhaus, known as the Eagle's Nest and built by the Nazis in 1938, sit high in the German Alps near Berchtesgaden. Gutted last month in a suspected arson attack on 23 October, the site has sparked debate about Germany's Nazi past amid rising far-right sentiment. Some argue it should be destroyed and returned to nature; others favour rebuilding or reconstructing parts, wary of Neo-Nazi pilgrimage. Isabel Heinemann says full reconstruction is out of the question but suggests documenting remains and adding modern design elements. Bavaria's Joachim Herrmann and Markus Blume support rebuilding without taxpayer cost. A 33-year-old man with a history of mental illness has been detained on suspicion of arson. The authorities have not commented on motive.

items.title: Priyanka Chopra Shares Diwali Celebrations With Nick Jonas And Malti

items.summary: A speeding Mahindra Thar, allegedly driven by a woman learning to drive, rammed a scooter in Kanpur on Saturday night, killing 55-year-old Santosh Singh Chauhan. Police said the three occupants abandoned the damaged SUV and fled in another car that arrived shortly after; eyewitnesses say it was speeding before crashing through walls. A case has been filed while police examine CCTV footage to identify the occupants.
items.title: Kanpur woman learner driver kills scooter rider on Diwali eve

items.summary: This guide explains seven Mixture-of-Experts routing strategies used in production and the models that use each one, from Softmax top-k (Mixtral) to Sigmoid gating with aux-loss-free bias balancing. It states loss-free balancing cut MaxVio from 0.72 to 0.04 at 1B, frames sigmoid plus bias as the current open default for frontier models in 2026, and notes expert choice leaks future tokens in causal LLMs, with DeepSeek researchers measuring an abnormal loss drop of about 10%. It advises reading config.json fields before serving rather than changing top-k at inference. The piece is written by Marktechpost AI Media Inc., which promotes its platform and newsletter.
items.title: MoE Routing Strategies Compared Across Open Models

items.summary: Prakhar Gupta argues India should focus on missile submarines capable of surviving a first strike, given reports that China has likely resumed producing bomb-grade uranium. Analysts note China's existing stock could arm roughly 670 warheads but may reach over 1,000 by 2030, raising questions about implications for India's nuclear deterrent.
items.title: India Should Prioritise Missile Submarines Amid China's Resumed Uranium Bomb Production

items.summary: According to a Financial Times report, Anthropic agreed to purchase commitments for roughly $3.4 billion worth of gas-fired generators supplying its data centers. The startup acquired 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty generator capacity from OnePWR Solutions in late September but did not buy the supplier itself or take on its staff; it gained engineering and construction services needed for installation. Reuters could not immediately verify the report, and neither Anthropic nor OnePWR responded to comment requests.
items.title: Anthropic Secures $3.4 Billion Generator Deal for Data Centers

items.summary: Union Minister HD Kumaraswamy released purported WhatsApp exchanges alleging bribes were sought to clear three stone crusher-related files in Karnataka’s Hassan district, including Rs 60 lakh. He said the chats covered land conversion and approvals, that Rs 75 lakh was paid to retain an official, and urged police to seize phones and investigate. No response came from authorities or the state government.
items.title: Karnataka Minister Releases Alleged Bribery WhatsApp Chats and Calls for Probe

items.summary: Livemint's Trisha Bhattacharya explains that while many people send traditional greeting messages during Diwali, WhatsApp stickers offer another way to share festive greetings. The guide covers three ways to obtain them: downloading built-in packs from the app's sticker store, creating customised designs directly in WhatsApp using gallery photos or text and emojis, and installing third-party applications from the Google Play Store for Android users. Availability of specific collections may vary by store and version. AI-generated stickers are offered in some countries but remain limited. Users can save favourite stickers to reuse later.
items.title: How to Find, Create and Send Diwali WhatsApp Stickers in 2026

items.summary: Current and former Microsoft employees are circulating an open letter, signed “Concerned Microsoft Workers,” accusing the company of prioritizing artificial intelligence over its staff, customers and climate commitments. The letter gained attention after Microsoft offered buyouts to about 60,000 workers, more than a quarter of its workforce, described as its largest such offer ever. Signatories cite mandatory AI tools, heavy workloads, constant reorganisations and threats from automation, alongside secretive data centre projects and contracts with ICE and the Israeli military. They demand worker input in AI decisions and reaffirm carbon-negative, water-positive and zero-waste goals by 2030. The claims come amid Microsoft’s reported $36. 6 billion profit and $45. 2 billion capital spending on data centres. In a note to staff, chief people officer Amy Coleman called the buyout “a new choice,” saying she does not link it to AI changes in work but did not rule out future layoffs.
items.title: Microsoft Workers Sign Open Letter Over AI-Driven Work Culture

items.summary: Police said a woman was held on Sunday for allegedly joining her son and his friends in assaulting a 17-year-old boy after he questioned obscene messages sent through an online gaming account. The attack occurred Saturday at the woman's rented house, leaving the boy injured; police registered a case under several sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
items.title: Woman arrested over assault tied to Instagram dispute in Kochi

items.summary: A Livemint article by Trisha Bhattacharya explains how ChatGPT and Google Gemini can transform uploaded photographs into festive portraits for Diwali. Users upload a clear image, describe outfits, backgrounds, colours and lighting, and ask the tools to preserve their facial features while adding traditional clothing, diyas, rangoli and warm lighting. The seven prompts shown range from elegant red-and-gold looks to glamorous Bollywood-inspired shoots. Results suit social media, greetings and personal photos. Editors warn that AI may not reproduce every facial detail accurately, so users should review images before sharing and obtain permission before editing someone else's photograph.
items.title: AI Prompts Turn Selfies Into Diwali Portraits

items.summary: Union Minister HD Kumaraswamy alleged on Sunday that officials in Hassan district demanded large sums to clear files and facilitate official work. He released what he described as 15 pages of purported WhatsApp conversations showing demands for money to clear crusher-related files and land conversion proposals. He said Rs 60 lakh was demanded, with Rs 50 lakh for a senior official and Rs 10 lakh distributed among staff; separately, Rs 75 lakh allegedly paid to retain an official in post. Kumaraswamy urged police to seize the phones used and investigate.
items.title: Union Minister Kumaraswamy Alleges Bribery in Hassan, Shares WhatsApp Chats

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India clarified that no changes are being made to existing CTS cheque books, contradicting social media messages claiming new standards and security features would take effect in 2027. RBI called the claims factually incorrect and misleading, advising people to rely only on its official communications for banking matters. The dates December 31, 2026 and 2027 were referenced in connection with these disputed messages.
items.title: RBI Clarifies No New Cheque Book Rules from January

items.summary: Google has open-sourced the Elephant-Goldfish Model (EGM) plugin, a design-and-review layer that makes an agent write a specification before any code is written. Fresh subagents with no conversation history then review that spec across five sequential stages: initial zoom out, comprehension test, critic review, intermediate zoom out, and implementation readiness. Google says thousands of its engineers use it, though the README states EGM is not officially supported and no accuracy benchmark has been published; adoption and harness test runs are cited as evidence instead. The best Codex 0.163.0 run completed 15 native fresh-context reviewers end to end in two live tests within 573.13 s, while some hosts still leak host instruction files into isolated reviewers.
items.title: Google Open-Sources Spec-First Coding Plugin for AI Agents

items.summary: Madan Kishor, a hospitality worker writing in a forum titled 'Make food and beverage recruitment ads clearer for applicants', argues that recent reports of restaurants offering attractive salaries reveal an opportunity to improve how such jobs are advertised. He says a headline salary alone is insufficient; applicants should also see working hours, meal-break coverage, split-shift details, pay components, rest arrangements, late-night shifts, training, and progression opportunities.
items.title: Hospitality worker proposes clearer food and beverage job ads

items.summary: A Year 1 student named Tiffany Ong Rou Ying, 13, shares that artificial intelligence is increasingly used in schools for learning materials and feedback. Students raise concerns about over-reliance, environmental impact, and the value of assignments when feedback is largely AI-generated. They suggest introducing AI gradually while preserving teachers' judgment and human connection.
items.title: Student Voices on AI in Schools Need Reassurance and Transparency

items.summary: This November 2026 comparison examines how ten open Mixture-of-Experts models route tokens, noting they agree only that each token selects its own experts while differing across five knobs: expert count (8 to 384), experts per token (top-k of 1 to 8), shared experts, the scoring function and load-balancing method. Sources are each model's Hugging Face config.json, card or report, verified November 7, 2026. Kimi K2 reportedly needed fewer FLOPs than sparsity-8 at equal loss; Llama 4 Maverick and gpt-oss leave gating or balancing unpublished.
items.title: Open MoE Models Differ on Routing Details Compared Across Ten Models

items.summary: After winning Tuesday’s midterm elections, Democrats say they will pursue aggressive investigations and legislation aimed at pressuring President Trump ahead of the 2028 election. Leaders such as Greg Casar, Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer outlined priorities including reimplementing Affordable Care Act subsidies, undoing Medicaid cuts, ending tariffs and confronting corruption—framed around three promises: lower costs, working government and cleaning up Washington. They explicitly ruled out a third impeachment of Trump, noting the Senate filibuster still blocks bills lacking 60 votes and that Trump remains in office until January 2029 with veto power. Schumer acknowledged he could block cost-reduction efforts but said voters would rebuke him if they did.
items.title: Democrats Map Legislative Agenda After Midterm Gains

items.summary: Amazon announced that US customers can now use its AI-powered assistant, Alexa for Shopping, to search products and complete purchases through text messages. The company said the feature lets users research items, track deals and price drops, and have purchases made on their behalf. It is rolling out first to a small group of invited customers before a broader launch in coming weeks.
items.title: Amazon Expands Alexa for Shopping With Text-Based Purchases

items.summary: Veteran Congress leader Sonia Gandhi and daughter Priyanka Gandhi revisited childhood Diwali celebrations in a social media conversation. Sonia described Ganesh idol rituals, diyas around the pond and roof, Kashmiri cuisine and sweet rice still made at home. She noted blue skies she said are rarely seen now. The memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love is scheduled to launch on November 10.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi recalls Diwali memories, memoir launch

items.summary: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy launched a personal attack on Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president KT Rama Rao, accusing him of forcing his sister out of the party over an unwillingness to share family property. Speaking at a women Self-Help Group meeting in Kodangal, he said KTR drove his sister Kavitha out after her release from jail for six months. He also questioned why any father but former chief minister K Chandrashekar Rao would treat Telangana unfairly during his 10-year tenure as asked by Revanth Reddy.
items.title: Revanth Reddy Attacks KTR Over Sister's Party Expulsion

items.summary: At the ninth China International Import Expo in Shanghai, from November 5-10, 2026, British-made teacups on display carry hand-painted scenes and touches of gold. The pieces draw on more than 200 years of British ceramic craftsmanship while reflecting Chinese tea's arrival in Britain during the 17th century, when imported porcelain inspired local potters. By the 19th century, afternoon tea had become a British ritual.
items.title: British teacups with Chinese tea heritage at CIIE 2026

items.summary: The Permanent Mission of China to the United Nations and Other International Organizations in Vienna hosted an event on Friday, November 6, 2026, marking the 55th anniversary of the restoration of the People's Republic of China's lawful seat in the UN. Li Song chaired it; nearly 200 participants attended. Speakers reflected on Resolution 2758 and reaffirmed commitment to multilateralism.
items.title: China Hosts UN Anniversary Event in Vienna

items.summary: The article explains how electric vehicle supply chains in Southeast Asia span continents, linking nickel from Indonesia and lithium from Chile with regional manufacturing expertise. It argues that economic value now lies in the connections between countries rather than single resources or factories. Indonesia, a leading nickel producer whose mined output rose an estimated 13% in 2025 per the US Geological Survey, is expanding domestic smelting to capture more industrial value. Southeast Asia's electric car sales more than doubled in 2025 to exceed half a million units, with Chinese brands making up over half of those sold, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). Chile and Canada are pursuing similar strategies: Asia received 95% of Chile's lithium exports in 2025 per its Subsecretariat of International Economic Relations, while Canada held 31 critical mineral processing facilities and 171 advanced projects as of March 2025.
items.title: Asia-Pacific Economies Build Integrated Electric Vehicle Supply Chains

items.summary: The Cop31 UN climate summit opens in Antalya, Turkey, with Australia presiding over negotiations following a compromise between the two competing host bids. Its host has said it must deliver “a tangible outcome … that people can see is real.” Scores of leaders from close to 190 countries gather as they confront what scientists describe as the strongest El Niño on record and temperatures surpassing the Paris Agreement’s 1.5C limit. Tensions are expected over climate finance, loss and damage, and slow emissions cuts. The US will again send no delegation, while more than 500 Australian scientists urge Australia to halt coal and gas approvals.
items.title: Turkey Hosts Cop31 Climate Summit Amid Global Pressure

items.summary: The article argues that last week’s US midterms reflected growing public resistance to AI, with dozens of measures limiting datacentre expansion passed. Heather Stewart frames the result as a wake-up call for tech leaders, attributing part of the Democrat wave to Trump-era cost-of-living pressures but emphasising anti-AI sentiment as a key driver. She notes the backlash may slow investment in AI’s physical infrastructure and accelerate an already-fragile market rethink. Quoting Capital Economics’ Joe Maher on late-cycle signs and TS Lombard’s Dario Perkins, she cites figures of $200bn current revenues supporting over $1tn future commitments from Anthropic and OpenAI as evidence the boom is unsustainable.
items.title: US Midterms Fuel Anti-AI Sentiment and Datacentre Backlash

items.summary: The Guardian published a cartoon by Tom Gauld about artificial intelligence and writing, accompanied by his account of the prompts he used to create it. The piece presents his own description of how he generated the image.
items.title: Tom Gauld Discusses Prompts Behind His AI and Writing Cartoon

items.summary: France announced it will be represented at United States-mediated talks with Russia and Ukraine scheduled for Nov 10 to 11 in Abu Dhabi, aimed at ending the war. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Europe's voice would be heard after President Trump suggested a broad deal involving all of Europe. The previously trilateral format may expand toward multilateral participation if progress is made.
items.title: France Confirms European Participation in US-Mediated Ukraine Talks

items.summary: Turkey will host climate negotiators from nearly 200 countries for annual talks at the UN’s 31st Conference of the Parties, opening Monday in Antalya. This follows a United Nations Environment Programme warning that steep emissions cuts are needed to limit warming to 1. 5C above pre-industrial levels. Recent electoral shifts offer optimism: Brazilian President Lula beat climate skeptic Flavio Bolsonaro and Brazil proposed roadmaps for fossil fuel weaning and deforestation reversal by 2030, while US Democrats gained majorities in the House and Senate after Tuesday’s midterms. Laurence Tubiana of the European Climate Foundation said COP31 could mark a pendulum shift as affected countries raise their voices. Turkey will focus talks on electrification to 35% of final energy consumption by 2035, France proposed cutting methane emissions 75% by 2035, and small island states are defending the 1. 5C goal.
items.title: Turkey Hosts COP31 Amid Climate Optimism After Brazil and US Electoral Shifts

items.summary: Culture secretary Lisa Nandy said the government is 'looking seriously' at adding second-hand reselling sites to its social media ban for under-16s, set to take effect in March next year. She cited keeping children safe from grooming risks. eBay welcomed constructive engagement while legislation details remain unclear; Vinted declined comment. The UK follows Australia's similar measure but intends a tougher enforcement approach.
items.title: UK Culture Secretary Considers Banning Under-16s From Vinted and eBay

items.summary: Chile's Atacama Desert is showing its largest floral display in about 30 years, possibly ever, after heavy El Niño rains brought the heaviest rainfall since records began in the 1950s. Floodwaters damaged dozens of homes and forced hundreds to evacuate before the bloom followed. More than 200 species are flowering across roughly 113,000 acres of Llanos de Challe National Park. Moisés Grimberg calls it a natural seed bank awakening with rain; Ana Sandoval of INIA's national seed bank says the desert is simply waiting for water. Tourism has surged: about 15,000 visitors so far versus roughly 10,000 annually, and around 300,000 overnight trips are expected over two months. Region governor Miguel Vargas seeks UNESCO World Heritage status to diversify an economy reliant on mining.
items.title: Atacama Desert's Rare Bloom Draws Record Visitors

items.summary: A WIRED writer recounts testing New York Times Cooking's new iOS-only beta feature that lets subscribers modify recipes with artificial intelligence. The tool appeared below an article announced on October 23, prompting backlash from commenters who threatened to cancel subscriptions; commenting was disabled after four days and roughly 172 angry comments.
items.title: WIRED Author Tests NYT Cooking's AI Recipe Modifier and Finds It Surprisingly Good

items.summary: About 800 people gathered in Tokyo on Sunday, including Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and family members of abductees such as Megumi Yokota, taken in 1977 at age 13. Speakers appealed for continued pressure until all return home while parents are still alive, and the rally adopted a resolution calling on North Korea to release them.
items.title: Tokyo rally of roughly 800 demands return of North Korea abductees

items.summary: This second story in a series on recovery from the August 8, 2023 Maui wildfires follows Mikey Burke as she attends acupuncture at the Lahaina Comprehensive Health Center while her family begins rebuilding its home. The Aug. 8 fires destroyed more than 2,200 buildings and killed more than 100 people; nearly 13,000 were displaced. Burke says survivors face a slow, unrelenting ordeal beyond physical loss, including mental health struggles and colonial injustice she calls "colonial inflammation." Her sons showed signs of post-traumatic stress disorder after the fires, but therapy through the Maui Wildfire Exposure Study brought their scores back to normal range. The study's lead researchers Ruben Juarez and Alika Maunakea secured new funding: an NIH grant of $2.2 million over three years for the HO'ĀLA-Maui initiative, plus a separate $3.6 million five-year award from the National Institutes of Health to study wildfire exposure effects on lung and heart health in 1,000 people. Juarez and Maunakea say these funds should keep the effort going after earlier funding was nearing an end."
items.title: Maui Wildfire Survivors Find Healing and Funding After Lahaina Fires

items.summary: Egypt reopened its embassy in Tripoli on Saturday during Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty's visit, marking a shift toward Libya's western government after years of backing eastern commander Khalifa Haftar. Talks covered trade and energy projects, plus Egypt's objections to a 2019 Turkey-Libya maritime agreement. Dbeibah praised Egyptian contributions to rebuilding Libya. Greece, Cyprus and the EU also oppose the deal.
items.title: Egypt Reopens Tripoli Embassy Amid Maritime Dispute Concerns

items.summary: Ruben Juarez and Alika Maunakea, University of Hawaiʻi professors who created the Maui Wildfire Exposure Study (MauiWES), spent a weekend in May running health screenings for survivors three years after the August 8, 2023 wildfires killed at least 102 people, displaced nearly 13,000 residents and destroyed more than 2,200 buildings. The study has grown to about 2,500 participants over three years, offering free testing, therapy, food assistance and insurance help; Juarez estimates more than 200 have gained private coverage through the effort. It found widespread emotional distress and linked poor lung function to elevated heavy metals in urine. Support is fraying: a state bill allotting $3 million failed at the last minute, earlier state funding totaled $2.3 million plus a $1.4 million federal grant, and renewal applications have gone unanswered for more than a year after staff cuts. The Department of Health disputed MauiWES’s findings, though the university said it was not claiming causation. Maunakea remains determined to continue despite feeling the study may be ending.
items.title: MauiWES Researchers Battle Funding Uncertainty Amid Lahaina Recovery

items.summary: The tragic shooting at Poland's Main Market Square in Krakow drew reactions worldwide, according to a news roundup of official responses. Leaders from Germany, France, Italy, Ukraine, the Baltic states, Spain, Romania, Hungary, the United Kingdom, the EU and the US offered condolences and stressed solidarity with Poland, repeatedly affirming that 'Poland does not stand alone.' Statements expressed shock at what officials called cowardly violence, extended sympathy to victims' families, wished recovery for the injured, thanked emergency services, and condemned all forms of terror. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Europe joins Poland in pain and solidarity, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described it as a shocking crime with no justification.
items.title: European and world leaders offer condolences after Krakow shooting

items.summary: After Karnataka's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, the size of the Muslim electorate shrank by 18.84 per cent (13.48 lakh), slightly above the state average; non-Muslims fell 17.79 per cent (86 lakh). The figures come from Sankalp, a political research consultancy, and are estimates because electoral rolls do not record religion. Analyst Sandeep Shastri told Frontline that Bengaluru's list was historically inflated by voters abroad or voting in their hometowns; around one-third of electors in select areas fit this pattern, he said. Deletions were larger for non-Muslims overall but greater for Muslims outside Bengaluru.
items.title: Karnataka Muslim Electorate Shrinks After SIR Revision

items.summary: Six people were killed and several others injured when a gunman opened fire in central Krakow, Poland's second largest city, on Saturday. BBC Verify authenticated footage showing about a dozen people running inside two buildings before police arrived. The suspect, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, was described by the interior minister as inspired by far-right ideologies; police said he used military weapons. Three more bodies were found at his home hours later.
items.title: How the deadly shooting in Krakow unfolded

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath reviewed his government's progress during Deepotsav celebrations in Ayodhya, highlighting infrastructural development, industrial growth, government jobs, expressways, action against Ram temple donation irregularities, and demolition drives. Addressing opposition strategies, he framed the electoral contest as a choice between supporters of security and law versus criminal elements.
items.title: UP Chief Minister Reviews Governance and Election Strategy During Ayodhya Event

items.summary: Australia defeated Samoa 44-12 at Sydney on Sunday night, advancing to the Rugby World Cup final. The Kangaroos controlled the match from the start as discipline and field position punished Samoa: three penalties, a set restart and a try fell within minutes of each other in the first half, leaving them with just two kicks for the last 19 minutes before Australia led 26-2 at the break. Adam Gee drew combined 12 restarts and penalties from Samoa. Reece Walsh raced clear on his hat-trick to stay in contention for Thursday's Golden Boot award. The result reinforced Australia's dominance, with only one loss from 18 starts since the set-restart era began and no home defeat in 11 years.
items.title: Australia Defeats Samoa in World Cup Final Semifinal

items.summary: The Lights of Shantinagar, Nidhi Arora's debut novel published by Penguin India, follows Sumi, an ambitious aspiring quantum physicist who arrives as a newlywed bride at the Kapoor household. The story explores how her scientific worldview is challenged by the unpredictable human relationships around her in the middle-class town of Shantinagar. Reviewers note that while the book builds nuanced characters and intricate interpersonal dynamics, it occasionally struggles with character consistency, particularly for figures like Pushpa, Chhotu, and Dhruv who lack fully developed arcs.
items.title: A debut novel on love and family in a quantum town

items.summary: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal defended his wearable device Temple on Sunday amid criticism over its Rs 85,000 price tag and scientific claims. In a detailed post on X, he said the product was designed for a global market and that he expected no more than 1% of its sales to come from India.
items.title: Zomato Founder Defends Temple Wearable Amid Price Criticism

items.summary: Pakistan Under-19 defeated arch-rivals India by three wickets at Al Amerat, Oman, on Sunday during the ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup 2026. Chasing 209 after being bowled out for 208 in 46.3 overs, Pakistan recovered from 63/5 through a century by captain Hamza Zahoor and a 107-run partnership with Hasnain Abbas Dar. Arjun Rajput's 107 off 85 deliveries gave India their total, supported by Kavya Patel (23). The win secured an important Group A result as Pakistan advanced toward the semi-finals.
items.title: Pakistan Under-19s beat India in U19 Asia Cup chase

items.summary: West Bengal's Suvendu Adhikari government unveiled a new industrial land procurement strategy under the West Bengal Investment Promotion Policy 2026, planning to buy land directly from owners and explore pooling. The move faces an early challenge in Purulia, where around 20 tribal organisations rallied at Patharkata on November 2 against industries threatening tribal rights over land, forests and water. Tribal leader Ratanlal Hansda warned that rare earth deposits estimated by the Geological Survey of India could intensify pressure on communities. Commentators caution fragmented holdings and a debt burden make implementation difficult.
items.title: Bengal's tribal land protests test new industrial policy

items.summary: In the November 8, 2026 Muhurat Trading ahead of Diwali, Indian equities rose sharply. Sensex climbed over 300 points to close at 81,349.31, while NSE's Nifty crossed 25,100 and reached 25,103.50 after gaining about 73 points. This marked the eighth consecutive session of gains as investors viewed the auspicious trading as lucky.
items.title: Indian markets rally in festive Muhurat Trading session

items.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, a retired Israel Defense Forces chief of staff from 2015 to 2019, has emerged as the principal challenger to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following the October 27 parliamentary elections that produced a hung parliament. On November 8, President Isaac Herzog granted Eisenkot the first opportunity to form a government after factions representing 67 Knesset members recommended him over 46 who backed Netanyahu. His candidacy reflects disagreements on accountability for the October 7 attacks, Gaza strategy, conscription of Haredim, far-right coalition partners and judicial independence. Analysts note that an Eisenkot government is unlikely to fundamentally alter India's bilateral relationship with Israel.
items.title: Eisenkot's Path to Challenging Netanyahu Amid Israeli Political Contest

items.summary: Diwali celebrations began on Sunday, with people across India and the global diaspora gathering to observe one of the most important festivals in the Hindu tradition. In Ayodhya, regarded as the birthplace of Lord Rama, festivities featured performances from the Ramayana, laser and light shows, live music, fireworks and drone displays.
items.title: Diwali Celebrations Marked Across India and the Global Diaspora

items.summary: The article explains how Niantic, the company that created Pokémon Go and sold it last year, has shifted toward building 'world models'—software that reconstructs physical environments from visual inputs to simulate physics. CTO Brian McClendon says they aim to rebuild the real world so robots can practice without moving physically. CEO Oliver Cameron of Odyssey contrasts language models with these systems, which predict a next image rather than a word. Jamie Shotton of Wayve notes cars need models that understand cause and effect. The piece also covers investment in startups like Advanced Machines Intelligence and World Labs, plus gig work collecting real-world footage for training data.
items.title: Niantic's ex-Pokémon Go maker pivots into AI world models

items.summary: Former Foreign Secretary David Lammy criticized the Home Office's handling of permanent residency applications from Turkish businesspeople, comparing their treatment to the Windrush scandal and calling it 'outrageous.' His remarks followed a Guardian report revealing hundreds of ILR refusals since early 2026 amid administrative review increases. Home Office figures obtained via freedom of information showed applications undergoing administrative review rose from 145 in 2025 to 395 between January and mid-August 2026, though the department maintains its rules have not changed.
items.title: Lammy Compares Treatment of Turkish Businesspeople to Windrush Scandal

items.summary: At a joint news conference in Shusha, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan reaffirmed Türkiye's support for Azerbaijan's efforts to establish lasting peace in the South Caucasus. He said the liberation of Karabakh had opened the door to a new era and praised ongoing reconstruction work. Aliyev called their unity 'eternal and unshakable,' recalling that both leaders stood with Azerbaijan throughout the 44-day Second Karabakh War in 2020.
items.title: Erdogan and Aliyev Reaffirm Türkiye-Azerbaijan Unity in Karabakh

items.summary: The Punjab Police brought gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi back to India from Ethiopia on Sunday, sources said. He is wanted in more than 30 heinous criminal cases and carried a ₹5 lakh reward announced by the Punjab government. Police described him as an alleged key kingpin of the Doni Bal-Prabh Dassuwal gang accused of directing targeted killings, extortion-related firing incidents and organised criminal networks while operating abroad. His name surfaced during investigation into an August 31 church attack in Tarn Taran; he was arrested after moving through the UAE, Kenya, Angola and Ethiopia as part of Operation SHAHID, a 10-month intelligence-led manhunt led by Punjab DGP Gaurav Yadav.
items.title: Punjab Gangster Afridi Arrested After International Manhunt

items.summary: Malaria control across Southern African Development Community (SADC) countries faces mounting pressure, with case numbers rising over the past two years. Four high-burden nations—Democratic Republic of Congo, Mozambique, Angola and Tanzania—together account for 22.9% of the global malaria burden. A speaker from South Africa argues that domestic funding must increase to fill intervention gaps by 2030. Threats include overstretched national programmes reliant on donor money, sudden US government funding cuts in 2025 that lowered Global Fund allocations by an average of 18%, and La Niña-driven flooding linked to a 55% case rise in Mozambique and 65,399 cases in Zimbabwe. The author calls for regional genomic hubs, early warning systems and sustained collaboration without implying these measures will succeed.
items.title: SADC Malaria Targets at Risk from Climate and Funding Cuts

items.summary: Researchers who study climate governance examined ten years of adaptation plans, laws and disaster-management frameworks from Burkina Faso, Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal and Sierra Leone ahead of COP31 in Türkiye. They found that the policies recognise costs to infrastructure and livelihoods but leave gaps around culture, mental health and community ties. The authors argue official assessments shape recovery budgets and requests for international support, so undocumented losses are less likely to be addressed. They recommend combining cost-based evaluations with input from affected communities before disasters strike, using existing agencies rather than new institutions.
items.title: West African climate plans price visible damage but miss invisible losses

items.summary: On Sunday, Poland launched a terrorism investigation into Saturday's mass shooting in Krakow, which killed six people and wounded many others. The 24-year-old gunman used a semi-automatic rifle while masked in military-style clothing; he remains in critical condition. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it an act of "terrorism", and the suspect was described as fascinated by far-right ideologies. Two police officers were injured, and three bodies found at his home later identified as relatives.
items.title: Poland opens terrorism probe after mass shooting in Krakow

items.summary: A strong earthquake struck central Japan on Sunday, shattering shop windows and prompting people to flee buildings across a wide area near Aichi Prefecture. The tourist city of Kyoto and the nearby prefecture of Yamanashi, home to Mount Fuji, were also affected. Local media reported that at least 22 people were injured. Following the quake, Japan's Meteorological Agency warned residents to brace for possible strong quakes in the coming week, especially over the next two to three days.
items.title: Earthquake Shakes Central Japan, Injuring at Least 22

items.summary: A scam circulating as a free grand piano offer from a recently widowed woman is an advance fee fraud, in which the sender requests payment for delivery of goods that never arrive. Victims typically pay around £300 after engaging with what appears to be a legitimate email. Piano dealer Forsyth says it has helped people avoid paying before delivery, while Sykes & Sons notes such scams are common and have affected musicians, churches and schools.
items.title: Piano giveaway emails lure victims into advance fee frauds

items.summary: Across Israel, people are divided over President Herzog's decision to appoint Gadi Eisenkot to lead the country's next government. The move struck a blow to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after he lost his parliamentary majority in last month's election. Yet one point unites everyone: forming a new government will not be easy.
items.title: Divided Israelis See Tough Road Ahead for New Government Formation

items.summary: A professor of innovation uses the 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper to explain how the Transformer reshaped artificial intelligence. He argues that today's industry still starts from an individual 'artificial worker,' leaving a gap before organizations reach enterprise performance, citing McKinsey's 2026 survey showing 80% reported improved personal productivity but only 37% saw positive enterprise EBIT.
items.title: Professor frames enterprise AI as waiting for its Transformer moment

items.summary: Art d'Egypte's 'Forever Is Now' exhibition, now in its sixth edition, is set against the Pyramids of Giza. The show runs until November 28 and features works by artists including Raphaele Shirley and Geoffroy Pithon. Its themes explore spatial order and cultural memory, prompting viewers to consider how the pyramids remain a reference for contemporary art after 4,500 years.
items.title: Giza pyramids host sixth 'Forever Is Now' art exhibition

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated Diwali with security personnel in Bastar, crediting their sacrifices for ending the Maoist insurgency and enabling development. He claimed every district is now free from Naxalism and that crores of citizens have overcome its fear, calling it the first such festival after a decades-long victory. For the first time in 47 years, no CRPF jawan died on duty last year. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh separately celebrated with Army personnel at Sherathang War Memorial near Nathula Pass in Sikkim.
items.title: Modi Spends Diwali With Security Forces Amid Claims of Naxalism Defeat

items.summary: Hamza Zahoor scored a hundred against India in the U19 Asia Cup, guiding Pakistan to a three-wicket win after India posted 209 runs. His winning boundary sparked celebrations as he pulled out a handwritten note reading 'Tomorrow match 50 Hamza Zahoor,' seemingly predicting his score before going one better with a magnificent century.
items.title: Pakistan star scores century and viral celebration

items.summary: Priyansh Patil and Parin Patil from Divaale Koliwada built a miniature mud fort featuring walls, bastions, gateways, Mavlas, cannons and decorative materials to revive the traditional Diwali practice of building forts. Their creation has drawn local appreciation as an effort to keep cultural heritage alive amid rising digital entertainment.
items.title: Two Boys Revive Maharashtra's Traditional Diwali Mud Fort-Making

items.summary: A journalist covering electric vehicles questions whether the industry is chasing the wrong products by focusing on large pickups and SUVs while ignoring 125cc-class combustion motorcycles, which he says are already highly efficient at around 100 mpg. He describes riding in Asia, noting that roads there run with small-displacement bikes used for work, school and cargo rather than as "motorcycle cultures" but transportation ones. He argues a light electric bike needs only about 4-6 kWh of battery, charges from an ordinary household outlet overnight without fast charging, costs around $160 per 10,000 km in electricity, and is approachable for riders who avoid heavy superbikes. A top comment by Porcupine adds that licensing a motorcycle requires months of planning compared with simply driving a car you are already licensed for, so he concludes the future may be giving the world's favorite motorcycle an electric motor rather than building another pickup truck.
items.title: An EV writer argues for electrifying small motorcycles first

items.summary: Mahi G, a conscious Adivasi rapper from Kalyan, rose through Indian hip-hop after her debut single Jungle Cha Raja was released in December 2021 and garnered 10,000 views within two days. The song celebrates the rallying cry of jal, jangal, zameen—water, forest, land—associated with Gond revolutionary Komaram Bheem. Ghane, a shy engineering graduate from Kalyan who recorded it after struggling to keep time on a metronome, has since released socially conscious tracks and collaborated with Greenpeace India in 2024. She remains independent and wary of label contracts amid fears that dissent invites repression. Mahi G is the winner of the South Asia Speaks Prize 2026, according to Mumbai-based critic Bhanuj Kappal, who wrote the profile.
items.title: Adivasi rapper Mahi G wins South Asia Speaks Prize

items.summary: EL PAÍS reconstructed how Mexico dismantled the criminal network behind the assassination of Uruapan mayor Carlos Manzo, a killing carried out on November 1, 2025. The investigation combined cellphone and hard-drive evidence with chat records from an encrypted Threema group called Ciudad, which had nine members created by El Licenciado to coordinate surveillance and prepare the attack. To date, according to information obtained by this newspaper, 34 suspects have been arrested, with at least five others still sought. Authorities linked El Licenciado to Ramón Álvarez Ayala, known as R1, a powerful CJNG figure tied to El Mencho. Investigators traced how municipal officials leaked Manzo's movements through the council chat and identified local commanders such as Comandante Caos, whose group had 16 people under his command at one point. By January of this year, prosecutors in Michoacán reported that the case was about 90% solved, with the remaining work focused on identifying the last members of the Ciudad group.
items.title: Mexico Unravels Cartel Network Behind Mayor Manzo's Killing

items.summary: More than 80% of global merchandise trade moves by sea, and the war launched alongside Israel against Iran has disrupted several strategic straits. The Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of world oil passed before the conflict, closed completely for the first time in history; analysts say higher shipping rates add more than $30 per barrel of oil. Traffic through Malacca fell sharply as well, and container volumes reached record highs in February but dropped 2.5% by July 2026 according to the World Trade Organization. War-risk insurance premiums for Hormuz have risen to between 3% and 10% of a vessel's value versus around 0.25% before the war, and an Oxford study estimated chokepoint disruptions cost about $192 billion annually. Tanker earnings exceeded $200,000 per day by late September. Analysts warn that restoring pre-conflict security will take time even after hostilities end.
items.title: Iran War Disrupts Global Shipping Through Key Chokepoints

items.summary: For the first time in more than three decades, the U.N. Security Council failed to renew its peacekeeping mission's mandate for disputed Western Sahara. The territory was a Spanish colony until 1975 and is largely controlled by Morocco, though it has long been claimed by the Algeria-backed Polisario Front and remains on the U.N. list of nonself-governing territories.
items.title: U.N. Security Council lets Western Sahara peacekeeping mandate lapse

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath criticized AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi for citing Abdul El-Sayed's win in the US Senate race to advocate Muslim political identity in Uttar Pradesh. Adityanath dismissed the idea of a Muslim chief minister and burqa-clad woman as prime minister, accusing Owaisi of pursuing an anti-India agenda with no place in the state.
items.title: Yogi Adityanath Rebuts Owaisi's 'Abdul Will Win in UP' Claim After Michigan Senate Victory

items.summary: A listicle presents five books addressing concerns about artificial intelligence, which the item describes as reshaping work, relationships, and society. The selections include Sherry Turkle's 'Artificial Intimacy,' Hamilton Mann's 'Trias Algorithmica: What Code Rules,' and Richard Socher's 'The Eureka Machine.' Each entry offers a summary or link to an Amazon listing, framing the books as perspectives on AI's promises and risks.
items.title: Five Books Offer Comfort for AI-Driven Existential Anxiety

items.summary: New Zealand's legislative election produced no clear winner, setting up weeks of political wrangling as the two main blocs seek a majority. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said his National Party won the most seats with 42 projected and had a mandate to form government, while opposition leader Chris Hipkins noted results were too close to call definitively. Minor parties gained record support, including Opportunity's seven seats that could make it a kingmaker. With final tallies due November 27, voters cited rising costs as their top concern, with one voter saying everything has gone up and the wealthy should pay more.
items.title: New Zealand Election Yields No Clear Winner

items.summary: A Fortune article reports that millennials, after roughly two decades of building careers with largely flat pay, are increasingly disillusioned and reconsidering their work. Glassdoor economist Chris Martin said millennial earnings have mostly peaked and will grow only as fast as inflation. A summer poll found 76% of millennials seriously rethinking career direction; the main barrier to nonprofit work is often prohibitive pay.
items.title: Millennials Reconsider Corporate Careers Over Nonprofits Amid Pay Plateau

items.summary: An article titled '5 awkward moments everyone has faced (and how to recover)' offers etiquette guidance for uncomfortable social situations. It notes that embarrassment often feels larger to the person experiencing it than to others, and that most slips cannot be prevented but responses can be controlled through honesty or a sincere apology. Reader's Digest provides advice across five scenarios: forgetting someone's name by asking them to remind you; sending an email to the wrong recipient by owning the mistake directly; letting a surprise slip before its time without inventing a larger lie; canceling plans then appearing elsewhere, which it calls especially rude and requiring honesty plus possibly treating the friend later; and misreading a greeting as a hug when offered a handshake. The common thread is not panicking, overexplaining, or turning one moment into a bigger production.
items.title: Reader's Digest Shares Ways to Recover From Awkward Moments

items.summary: President Isaac Herzog has tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new Israeli government, per his office's Saturday statement. The move follows the October election, in which Eisenkot's anti-Netanyahu bloc won 48 of parliament's 120 seats to Netanyahu's camp's 53, while Arab parties secured 19 historic seats. Eisenkot has 28 days—extendable by Herzog for up to 14—to gather the 61 votes needed, after which talks are expected to be complicated.
items.title: Herzog Names Eisenkot Israel's Next Prime Minister
